title: Registration, revalidation and fitness to practise
blurb: Know exactly what a midwife needs to revalidate every three years, and how the NMC acts when fitness to practise is in question.
question: A midwife is due to revalidate next month. She has 520 practice hours, 35 hours of CPD (12 participatory), five pieces of feedback and five reflective accounts. What must she do before submitting?

teach.body: Only a registered midwife (or a registered medical practitioner) may attend a woman in childbirth, except in sudden or urgent necessity or as a recognised student. To keep that registration, midwives renew it and revalidate with the NMC every three years. Revalidation shows you are keeping up to date and practising safely in line with the Code. In plain English: it is your three-yearly proof that you still meet the standard. It is not itself an assessment of fitness to practise.
teach.cite: Nursing and Midwifery Order 2001 art 45; NMC revalidation requirements

items.label: CPD, of which at least 20 participatory
pieces of feedback and reflective accounts

teach.caption: Dual registration as nurse and midwife needs 900 hours (450 in each); triple registration 1,350.

head: Requirement
Detail
rows: 5, on the NMC form, linked to the Code
teach.caption: Participatory CPD means learning with one or more other professionals, in person or virtually.

teach.h: Reflection is the heart of it
teach.body: SPM 1.27 asks midwives to take responsibility for continuous self-reflection and to seek and respond to feedback. The five reflective accounts can be based on CPD, feedback or an event, and each is linked to the Code. They need not be long or academic. The reflective discussion must be with another NMC registrant; if your confirmer is not on the NMC register, that discussion is held separately before confirmation. Never record anything that could identify a woman or baby.

teach.h: If you are short of practice hours
Grounds for impaired fitness to practise
teach.caption: A register entry obtained fraudulently or made incorrectly is a separate kind of allegation.
Striking off cannot be used for lack of competence, health or English alone until the person has been suspended or on conditions for at least two continuous years.

teach.body: Folake, a community midwife, has 520 practice hours, 35 CPD hours and five reflections, but only 12 of her CPD hours were participatory. She is 8 participatory hours short. She should complete more participatory learning, such as a multidisciplinary skills drill or a peer-led study session, before submitting. Her reflective discussion must be with another NMC registrant, and she must declare any caution or conviction in her health and character declaration.

teach.text: Being off sick, or having a disability or long-term condition, does not in itself mean a midwife's fitness to practise is impaired. The NMC acts where there is a risk to the public. Equally, revalidation is not a fitness to practise assessment: they are different processes.

items: Revalidate every 3 years: 450 midwifery hours (900 dual, 1,350 triple), 35 CPD hours with at least 20 participatory.
5 pieces of practice-related feedback, 5 reflective accounts on the NMC form, a reflective discussion with an NMC registrant.
Health and character declaration, professional indemnity (Code 12.1) and confirmation complete it.
Impairment grounds: misconduct, lack of competence, conviction or caution, health, English, another regulator's finding.
Sanctions: caution (1 to 5 years), conditions (up to 3 years), suspension (up to 1 year), striking off.

summary: You can now list every revalidation requirement with its numbers and spot when a midwife is not ready to submit. You can also name the legal grounds for impaired fitness to practise and the sanctions the NMC can impose.

A.q: How many practice hours must a midwife with a single registration complete in the three years before revalidation?
A.why: A single registration (midwife) needs 450 practice hours in the three-year period.

whyNot.1: 900 hours applies to dual registration as a nurse and midwife.
whyNot.2: 350 hours is below the NMC requirement.

A.q: Of the 35 hours of CPD needed for revalidation, how many must be participatory?
A.why: At least 20 of the 35 CPD hours must be participatory, involving interaction with one or more other professionals.

whyNot.0: 10 hours is below the NMC requirement.
whyNot.1: 15 hours is below the NMC requirement.
whyNot.3: 25 hours exceeds the minimum; the requirement is at least 20.

A.q: A midwife's line manager, who is a physiotherapist, will confirm her revalidation. Who must she have her reflective discussion with?
options: Any senior member of the trust
A student midwife she has mentored
A.why: The reflective discussion must be with another NMC registrant. If the confirmer is not on the NMC register, the discussion is held separately before confirmation.

whyNot.0: The physiotherapist can confirm, but is not an NMC registrant, so cannot hold the reflective discussion.
whyNot.2: Seniority is not the test; the person must be on the NMC register.
whyNot.3: A student midwife is not yet on the NMC register.

B.q: A midwife is charged with a criminal offence unrelated to work. According to the Code, what should she do?
options: Tell the NMC at her next revalidation
Wait for the court verdict before telling anyone
Tell the NMC and her employer as soon as she can
Tell her employer, who will inform the NMC
B.why: Code 23.2: tell the NMC and employers as soon as you can about any caution or charge, conditional discharge or conviction (other than a protected one).

whyNot.0: Waiting until revalidation is too late; the duty is to tell them as soon as she can.
whyNot.1: The duty covers charges, not just convictions.
whyNot.3: She must tell the NMC herself as well as her employer.

B.q: Which of these is a ground on which a midwife's fitness to practise can be found impaired under the Nursing and Midwifery Order 2001?
B.why: Article 22 includes not having the necessary knowledge of English, alongside misconduct, lack of competence, conviction or caution, health and another regulator's determination.

whyNot.0: A complaint may lead to investigation, but it is not itself one of the statutory grounds.
whyNot.2: A CPD shortfall means she cannot revalidate; it is not an impairment ground.
whyNot.3: Part-time working is not a ground, provided she still meets the practice hours.

B.q: A midwife has been on long-term sick leave with depression and is now returning to work. Which statement about her fitness to practise is correct?
options: It is impaired until a doctor clears her
She must self-refer to the NMC first
Sick leave does not mean it is impaired
She must re-sit the Test of Competence
B.why: NMC guidance: being signed off sick, or having a long-term condition, does not necessarily mean fitness to practise is impaired. The NMC acts where there is a risk of harm.

whyNot.0: Health becomes an FtP issue only where it creates a risk to the public.
whyNot.1: There is no requirement to self-refer simply because of sick leave.
whyNot.3: The Test of Competence is for returning to the register, not returning from sick leave.

C.q: A midwife has five reflective accounts, 35 CPD hours (22 participatory) and 480 practice hours. Two pieces of her feedback name the women involved. What should she do before submitting?
options: Submit, as the numbers are all met
Ask the women to consent to being named
Remove identifying details from the feedback
Replace them with feedback from colleagues
C.why: Revalidation records must not include information that could identify a person. She anonymises the feedback; her numbers already meet the requirements.

whyNot.0: The numbers are met, but identifiable information must be removed first.
whyNot.1: Consent is not the route; the NMC asks that records are not identifiable.
whyNot.3: Feedback can come from any source, so there is no need to replace it, only to anonymise it.

C.q: A midwife registered in 2023 worked 300 hours as a midwife in the last three years because of a career break. What is the correct next step?
options: Revalidate and make up hours next cycle
Complete a return to practice programme
Ask her confirmer to approve the shortfall
Count her CPD hours as practice hours
C.why: If practice hours are not met, she cannot revalidate. The routes are a return to practice programme or the Test of Competence before renewal.

whyNot.0: Hours cannot be carried forward; the requirement must be met to revalidate now.
whyNot.2: A confirmer cannot waive a requirement.
whyNot.3: CPD hours are a separate requirement and do not count as practice hours.

C.q: A Fitness to Practise Committee finds a midwife's practice impaired by lack of competence. She has had no previous sanctions. Which order is NOT available to the committee at this stage?
C.why: Article 29(6): striking off for lack of competence, health or English requires at least two years' continuous suspension or conditions immediately before the decision.

whyNot.0: A caution order (1 to 5 years) is available.
whyNot.1: Conditions of practice (up to 3 years) are available.

reteach.title: Revalidation as a three-year portfolio
reteach.question: Imagine your revalidation as a folder you build over three years. What goes in it?

blocks.body: Log practice hours each year. Record CPD with method, topic, dates, hours, link to practice and the relevant part of the Code. Save five pieces of feedback (anonymised) and write a reflective account soon after each learning moment. Near the end, hold your reflective discussion with an NMC registrant, complete your health and character declaration and indemnity, then get confirmation.

blocks.text: The two fives: 5 pieces of feedback AND 5 reflective accounts. The two numbers people swap: 35 total CPD hours versus 20 participatory.

explain.body: 450 practice hours as a midwife (900 for nurse and midwife). 35 hours CPD, at least 20 participatory: learning that involves interaction with other professionals, in person or virtual.

test.q: A midwife and nurse with dual registration is revalidating. How many practice hours does she need in total?
test.why: Dual registration needs 900 hours: 450 for each registration.

whyNot.1: 450 hours is for a single registration.
whyNot.2: 675 hours is not an NMC figure.

explain.body: Five pieces of practice-related feedback from any source; five written reflective accounts on the NMC form, each linked to the Code; a reflective discussion with another NMC registrant.

test.q: What must each of a midwife's five written reflective accounts be linked to?
test.why: Each reflective account relates to CPD, feedback or an event and to the Code.

whyNot.0: Reflective accounts need not be academic or reference research.
whyNot.1: They are not tied to a trust policy.
whyNot.3: A development plan may help, but the NMC requirement is the link to the Code.

explain.body: Health and character declaration (including charges, cautions and convictions), an appropriate indemnity arrangement (Code 12.1), and confirmation by an appropriate confirmer, usually the line manager.

test.q: Which document does Code standard 12 require every midwife to have in place?
test.why: Code 12.1: have an appropriate indemnity arrangement relevant to your scope of practice.

whyNot.0: A development plan is useful but not Code standard 12.
whyNot.2: Clinical supervision is supportive, not a Code 12 requirement.
whyNot.3: Practice assessor arrangements relate to student assessment.

explain.body: Impairment grounds (art 22): misconduct, lack of competence, conviction or caution, physical or mental health, not having the necessary English, another regulator's determination. Sanctions (art 29): caution, conditions, suspension, striking off.

test.q: What is the maximum period for a suspension order made by the Fitness to Practise Committee?
test.why: Article 29(5)(b): a suspension order is for a specified period not exceeding one year.

whyNot.0: Six months is within the limit but is not the maximum.
whyNot.1: Up to three years is the limit for a conditions of practice order.
whyNot.2: Up to five years is the limit for a caution order.
